clarity.justification: The method directly addresses the hypothesis by comparing four query types with a common pipeline and explicit measurements, including “LocalizationScore = 1 - (min #contiguous layers to recover 90% of clean logit diff)/depth,” MLP/attention reliance, peak depth, and patching-profile correlation. The prediction is directional—“factual most localized/MLP/mid-layer; conceptual+relational distributed/attention; procedural latest-layer”—so failure to observe that ordering, or observing its reversal, would refute the stated spectrum, although the claim weakens this somewhat by saying that “a graded or model-dependent spectrum is still a publishable, informative result.” Some operational details remain ambiguous, especially whether the proposed conceptual and procedural prompts genuinely instantiate knowledge matched to the same base fact and exactly how “attention-knockout” deltas are made commensurable with MLP ablations, but the core comparisons and statistical analysis are clear.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is to “instantiate each [base fact] in 4 matched query types,” particularly constructing valid procedural step-sequences and relational two-hop questions while controlling surface form; this is custom benchmark-design work rather than a magic step, but the proposal gives only examples and not a complete construction or validation rule. The named artifacts and methods—CounterFact, T-REx, Pythia, Qwen2.5, Llama-3, linear probes, activation patching, ROME, and MEMIT—exist and are supported by standard interpretability and deep-learning tooling, though applying “ROME/MEMIT-style edits per type” beyond factual associations needs additional specification. Resources are usefully quantified as “~4k base facts,” four query types, “4 paraphrases,” distractor variants, and seven named model configurations, while controls for a runnable negative result include clean-versus-corrupted patching, paraphrases, distractors, constituent-fact verification, and mixed-effects comparisons across entities and models.
